problem: The eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 2k\end{aligned}]$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =k+2$ is  $[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ k-1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Value of an Unknown Given an Eigenvalue and Eigenvector of a Matrix
examples.problem: An eigenvector of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071103/assets/f5ac973d5d7dd390f8cf9231515815f334d0c01dafeab14ba58fef25db4a8e8d.png) corresponding to an eigenvalue $\lambda=6c$ is  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071103/assets/a7e303f19be04db829faaa41133c70d7b6e5647ed75063674ca564a2952c09eb.png) Determine the value of $c.$
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $\mathbf{v}$ such that $A\mathbf{v}=\lambda \mathbf{v}.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2c\end{aligned}] & =6c[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2c\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2+2c \\ 1+4c\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6c \\ 12{c}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2+2c=6c \\ 1+4c=12{c}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $c$ in the first equation, we get

$$
2+2c=6c \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad c = \dfrac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, substituting $c=\dfrac{1}{2}$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1+4c & =12{c}^{2} \\ 1+4\cdot \frac{1}{2} & =12{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\ 3 & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a true statement.

Therefore, the solutions of the system is $c=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

The vector $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $C$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $-4.$ Find the vector $Cv.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-4.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Cv & =-4v.\end{aligned}
$$
